classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two output percentages using different input masses, then interpret their comparison as efficiency.

content.prompt:
Two different machines are used to produce chocolates in a chocolate shop.

Machine A produces $520\text{ g}$ of chocolate from $650\text{ g}$ of raw materials. Machine B produces $450\text{ g}$ of chocolates from $600\text{ g}$ of raw materials. The rest of the raw materials stick to the machines.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What percentage, by weight, of the raw materials is turned into chocolates by machine A?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by A}&=\frac{520}{650}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by A}&=\frac45\times100\%\\\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by A}&=80\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage, by weight, of the raw materials is turned into chocolates by machine B?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by B}&=\frac{450}{600}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by B}&=\frac34\times100\%\\\text{Percentage turned into chocolates by B}&=75\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Which of the machines is the more efficient?

answer.worked: Machine A is more efficient because it turns $80\%$ of its raw materials into chocolates, compared with $75\%$ for machine B.
